intro: You are standing in the Ancient City of Stratonikeia, in Muğla province, at Eskihisar near Yatağan. Its story begins in the 3rd century BC. Vast and built of marble, it carries a memorable nickname: the 'City of Gladiators'.
history: Long before its marble streets, the settlement was known as Atriya in Hittite times. After 281 BC it was renamed after Stratonike, wife of the Seleucid king Antiochus I. In the Hellenistic and Roman periods it was a major Carian city, and under Rome it housed a renowned gladiator school. And here life never stopped: the city remained continuously inhabited through the Byzantine, Beylik and Ottoman periods.
structure-2: You are now at the Serapeum, a sanctuary and temple complex dedicated to the Egyptian god Serapis. Imagine worshippers arriving here, far from Egypt, to honour a god from the banks of another world.
structure-4: Before you rises the North City Gate, the monumental entrance on the north side of the city. Stand beneath it for a moment and feel how it was meant to impress everyone who arrived.
structure-5: These are the City Walls, the defensive circuit that once encircled Stratonikeia. Follow their line with your eyes and picture the city they protected.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre and the Gymnasium.
facts: Did you know? The city is nicknamed the 'City of Gladiators' because gladiatorial games were held in its huge theatre. Later, an Ottoman village was built inside the ancient city: the houses, coffee house and fountain of Eskihisar stand among ancient columns, two layers living inside each other. Its north gate is one of the largest ancient city gates in Anatolia. And the name? It comes from the Seleucid queen Stratonice, the woman at the centre of a famous story about her marriages within the royal house.
outro: This brings our journey through Stratonikeia to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Gladiators, villagers and kings have all passed through here; let the stones wait for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
